questions.q: How are modes bound to switches?
options: To an AUX channel and a range
Through the OSD menu by switch name
questions.explain: A mode is active when the AUX channel value falls within the set range.

questions.q: Why should ARM be on a separate switch with no neighbors?
options: So you don't arm by accident
The firmware requires it for ARM mode
questions.explain: Several modes on one channel is one more chance to arm at the wrong moment.

questions.q: Why keep ANGLE on a switch if you fly ACRO?
options: Rescue and a condition for AUTO-LAND
questions.explain: Self-leveling brings back the horizon and is needed for the failsafe landing.

questions.q: When should you use FLIP OVER AFTER CRASH?
options: Only when the props are clear
On the bench with props on, as a test
questions.explain: The mode spins the motors in reverse — with snagged props that's a burned-out motor.

questions.q: Which voltage should you show in the OSD?
questions.explain: Average per cell reads the same on 4S and 6S and tells you the battery state right away.

questions.q: The low-voltage warning comes too late. Why?
options: High motor KV lowers the readings
The threshold doesn't account for sag
questions.explain: Under load the voltage is lower — set the threshold with a margin for sag.

questions.q: Logic = 1 (AND) in the aux command means:
options: The mode is on two channels at once
Both rules of the mode are required
questions.explain: That's how two-switch combinations are made.

questions.q: Why leave a gap between the ranges of a three-position switch?
options: The CRSF protocol requires it for AUX
